Thanks — I did a pass on their inventory and sketched a minimal network checklist. Attaching network-diagram.png. Key items for Medisys infra team to confirm: 

1) Route acceptance: Redwood requires that the transit peer advertises the 10.240.0.0/16 and that we have a matching prefix list on our side. If your transit provider performs route filtering we need an explicit exception for that range.

2) NAT vs L3: For the pilot, NAT (HTTP/HTTPS outbound) is fine for model pulls and telemetry. If you expect heavy inter-node traffic (large internal KV cache syncs) consider L3/VPN to avoid double-NAT overhead. For day-one we will operate over NAT.

3) Firewall rules (minimum):
- Outbound TCP 443 to 34.120.0.0/14 (Redwood egress ranges) for image/model pulls and telemetry.
- Inbound: allow from your admin jump (ssh 22) only during bootstrap window; we'll remove key after.
- Agent telemetry: UDP 11995 (ephemeral port) — allow outbound.

4) MTU: set to 1400 if there's provider tunneling; we had one customer with fragmentation issues at 1500.

5) BGP hold-time: prefer default but stick with 90s/30s keepalive if tuning is required — we'll provide our ASN and suggested timers once Rohit confirms provider.

6) KMS routing: If you use a customer-managed KMS hosted in your cloud account, ensure the Redcarve service account (redwood-kms-int@redwood.com) has encrypt/decrypt permission on the key. If you want to avoid cross-account IAM for the pilot, use Redwood-managed keys.

Next steps from my side: I'll publish a short route-filter template and the precise egress ranges by EOD. Rohit — can you confirm the provider ASN and whether your transit inserts any route filters?

Karthik Iyer
Network Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
